sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header for the maamar from Shabbos Tavo, 18 Elul 5730.

translations.translation: B'Siyata D'Shmaya.
Shabbos Parshas Tavo,
18 Elul,

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that just as Hashem makes Israel one nation, so too Israel makes Hashem one in the world through their declaration of His unity.

translations.translation: "You have distinguished [or declared] Hashem today... and Hashem has distinguished you today..."
And it is brought in the Gemara:
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: "You have made Me a single entity in the world, as it is said,
'Hear O Israel, Hashem our G-d, Hashem is One.' And I will make you a single entity in the world, as it is said,
'And who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land.'"
And it is necessary to understand what they said, "You have made Me a single entity,"
for the explanation of "You have made Me" etc. is,
that this—that Hashem is One
(a single entity)—
is brought about by Israel.
And this is also understood from the fact that they compare "I will make you" etc. to "You have made Me"
(and especially according to the version
"I too will make"),
for just as the explanation of "I will make you" etc. is that this—that Israel are one nation—is brought about by the Holy One, blessed be He,
[as the verse continues
(after it says "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land")
"which G-d went Himself to redeem for Himself a people,"
and Rashi explains:
"And from what are they distinguished from all the nations?
From this, that G-d went Himself to redeem for Himself a people... from this we are distinguished."]
So too is the explanation of "You have made Me" etc.,
that the matter of "Hashem is One" is brought about by Israel.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the praise of G-d in His tefillin is specifically the praise of Israel's own virtue, which is a greater glory than the praise Israel gives to Him.

translations.translation: Now, the above explanation of "you have distinguished" and "has distinguished you"
("You have made Me a single entity in the world, and I will make you a single entity in the world")
comes as a continuation of what is brought in the Gemara
(before this):
"The tefillin of the Master
of the Universe—what is written in them?... 'And who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land.'
And does the Holy One, blessed be He, take pride in the praise of Israel?
Yes,
for it is written, 'You have distinguished Hashem today,' and it is written, 'And Hashem has distinguished you today.'
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: 'You have made Me a single entity in the world, and I will make you a single entity in the world.'"
And the explanation of this
(in the Gemara's question, "Does the Holy One, blessed be He, take pride in the praise of Israel?")
is that tefillin are called "glory,"
as it is said,
"Bind your glory upon you,"
for tefillin bring glory and praise to the person who dons them.
And so too is it with the tefillin of the Master of the Universe, that they bring Him glory and praise, as it were.
And from this it is understood
that "Who is like Your people Israel" etc., which is written in the tefillin of the Master of the Universe,
is the glory and praise of the Holy One, blessed be He.
And this is what the Gemara questions: "Does the Holy One, blessed be He, take pride in the praise of Israel?"
For this verse
("And who is like Your people Israel" etc.)
is the praise of Israel,
so how can it be the glory and praise of the Holy One, blessed be He?
And it answers: "Yes,
for it is written, 'You have distinguished Hashem,'"
"Distinguished" being a term of importance and praise,
meaning that Israel effect importance and praise in the Holy One, blessed be He.
And it is necessary to understand,
for the proof from the verse "You have distinguished Hashem" is
(seemingly)
only that the Holy One, blessed be He, takes pride through the praises that Israel praise Him, may He be exalted
("Hashem our G-d, Hashem is One"),

for although all creations are utterly incomparable to Him, may He be exalted, nevertheless it arose in His will, may He be exalted, that through the praises that Israel praise Him, there should be brought to Him
(as it were)
importance and praise.
And how is it proven from this that the Holy One, blessed be He, takes pride in the praise of Israel,
in the praise of Israel's virtue,
that Israel are one nation in the land?
And it must be said,
that through "You have distinguished Hashem,"
that Israel praise the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Holy One, blessed be He, takes pride in this,
through this it is brought about that the Holy One, blessed be He, takes pride in the very praise of Israel.
And it should be added,
that from the fact that the verse written in the tefillin of the Master of the Universe is
(not the verse "Hear O Israel" etc. "Hashem is One"
(as in our tefillin),
but rather)
the verse "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land,"
it is proven
that this praise of the Holy One, blessed be He,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, takes pride in the praise of Israel,
is a greater praise than the praise of "You have distinguished Hashem"
(the praise of Hashem through Israel praising Him).
To the extent that this praise
(that He takes pride in the praise of Israel themselves)
is
(the tefillin)
His glory.
Also, it is necessary to understand what the Tzemach Tzedek, our master, brings
(in his maamar beginning "You have distinguished Hashem today"),
that regarding the matter of "you have distinguished" and "has distinguished you" there are two opinions.
For the Rashba
wrote that "you have distinguished" and "has distinguished you" is in the manner of "My Beloved is mine and I am His,"
and the Maharsha
wrote that it is in the manner of "I am my Beloved's and my Beloved is mine."
And it is necessary to understand,
for the order of "you have distinguished" and "has distinguished you"
("you have distinguished" and then "has distinguished you")
is analogous to "I am my Beloved's"
(and then)
"and my Beloved is mine,"
so what is the reason of the Rashba that "you have distinguished" and "has distinguished you" is in the manner of "My Beloved is mine and I am His"?
